rights.title: Your rights as a parent
rights.description: Hi! We're here to help you understand your child's Individualized Education Program (IEP) better. Navigating this process can feel overwhelming, but you have important rights as a parent. Here are some things you should know:
rights.bulletPoints.1: You can request a translator for IEP meetings to ensure clear communication.
rights.bulletPoints.2: You have the right to take your time before signing an IEP - you don't need to sign until you're ready.
rights.bulletPoints.3: You can consent to all, some, or none of the proposed services - your child won't receive new services without your approval.
rights.bulletPoints.4: You have the right to request an IEP meeting at any time, not just at the annual review, and the school must schedule it within 30 days.
rights.bulletPoints.5: If an administrator isn't present at the meeting, you have the right to reschedule for a time when they can attend.
rights.bulletPoints.6: By law, your case manager must provide you with a booklet of your parental rights before the IEP meeting.

about.title: About the AIEP Tool
about.aiepDescription: AI for IEPs (AIEP) is a free, open-source and AI-powered tool designed to help families understand and use Individualized Education Programs (IEPs).
about.builtWith: Built with parents and caregivers in California, the tool helps families:
about.helpsFamilies.understand: Understand complex educational and legal terms through plain-language explanations
about.helpsFamilies.summaries: Get clear summaries of key goals, services, and priorities
about.helpsFamilies.prepare: Prepare questions and resources for IEP meetings
about.ourGoal: Our goal is simple: to help families feel informed, confident, and empowered to advocate for their children's education.
about.developedBy: AIEP was developed by an interdisciplinary team of educators, designers, researchers, and technologists, working closely with a core group of Parent Navigators.
about.parentNavigatorsList.codesigned: Co-designed the tool based on real family needs
about.parentNavigatorsList.tested: Tested and shaped what the tool does (and doesn't do)
about.parentNavigatorsList.canvassers: Served as canvassers and ambassadors, helping other families learn about and use AIEP while bringing their feedback back to the programmers and designers.
about.livedExperience: Their lived experience guided every step of development.
about.biggerProjectDescription: AIEP is part of a broader Community-Centered AI project, the Burnes Center for Social Change and its AI for Impact program, and Innovate Public Schools. Together we explore how AI in public systems can be built with communities, not just for them.
about.learnMoreProject: Learn more about the project, research, and resources on our project's information page.
about.supportedBy: The project was supported by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative in 2025.
about.description: AI-IEP makes Individualized Education Program documents easier to understand through AI-powered translation, simplified language, and helpful resources for parents.
about.thankYouAdvocating: Thank you for advocating for children's right to education!
about.thankYouMessage: Your dedication to understanding and navigating your child's IEP makes a real difference. Together, we're ensuring every child has access to the quality education they deserve.
about.innovatePublicSchoolsDescription: Innovate Public Schools is a nonprofit organization dedicated to building the capacity of parents and families to organize, advocate, and demand high quality schools for their children.
about.theGovLabDescription: The GovLab's mission is to improve people's lives by changing the way we govern. Our goal is to strengthen the ability of institutions – including but not limited to governments – and people to work more openly, collaboratively, effectively and legitimately to make better decisions and solve public problems.

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy for The GovLab AIEP
privacyPolicy.intro: At The GovLab, we take your privacy seriously. This policy outlines how we handle, use, and protect your information when you use the AIEP application.
privacyPolicy.iepDocuments.title: How We Handle Your Individualized Education Program (IEP) Documents
privacyPolicy.iepDocuments.subtitle: Documents
privacyPolicy.iepDocuments.item1: When you upload an IEP PDF, we immediately create a text version using OCR (Optical Character Recognition) and delete the original PDF right away.
privacyPolicy.iepDocuments.item2: We do not store any PDFs of IEPs.
privacyPolicy.iepDocuments.item3: Before anything is processed further, we run the text through a tool from AWS that removes personal information: names, addresses, social security numbers and phone numbers. Every name is replaced, including your child's. (Using AWS Comprehend)
privacyPolicy.iepDocuments.item4: Only this cleaned-up version of the IEP is sent to our language models. Your child's name is added back into the summary afterwards, from the name you gave us, so no name is sent to the models at any point.
privacyPolicy.languageModels.title: The Language Models We Use
privacyPolicy.languageModels.item1: We use Mistral's enterprise version and the OpenAI API for language processing.
privacyPolicy.languageModels.item2: Neither company trains their AI models using the documents we send them. Your data stays private and is not reused for any future AI training.
privacyPolicy.security.title: How We Keep Everything Secure
privacyPolicy.security.intro: We have strong protections in place at every level:
privacyPolicy.security.access.title: Access and Identity Protection
privacyPolicy.security.access.item1: Role-based access control and multi-factor authentication:
privacyPolicy.security.access.item1.desc: Only the right people can access systems, and they must verify their identity.
privacyPolicy.security.access.item2.desc: Your data is protected both when it's being sent between services and when it's stored.
privacyPolicy.security.access.item3.desc: We keep detailed logs to track access and actions for security and accountability.
privacyPolicy.security.infrastructure.it: Our systems are built in a repeatable, reviewable way.
We keep development and live environments separate to prevent accidental leaks.
All code changes go through automated testing and tracking before being deployed.
privacyPolicy.security.monitoring.title: Monitoring and Response
We watch for security threats and can act quickly.
If something happens, we have a clear process to investigate and fix it.
privacyPolicy.security.problems.title: Finding and Fixing Problems Early
privacyPolicy.security.problems.item1.de: We regularly scan our systems for vulnerabilities.
privacyPolicy.security.problems.item2.de: Passwords and sensitive configuration details are securely stored and protected.
privacyPolicy.security.sensitive.title: Extra Steps for Handling Sensitive Information
privacyPolicy.security.sensitive.item1.d: Only people who absolutely need to see PHI can access it.
privacyPolicy.phoneNumbers.title: How We Handle Phone Numbers (SMS Consent & Use)
privacyPolicy.phoneNumbers.item1: We only ask for your phone number if you choose to create an account using your phone instead of an email address.
privacyPolicy.phoneNumbers.item2: We do not use your phone number for any purpose other than sending you One-Time Passcodes (OTPs) to verify your identity.
privacyPolicy.phoneNumbers.item3: We never share or sell phone numbers, and we do not use them for marketing or communication outside of login verification.
privacyPolicy.phoneNumbers.item4: Phone numbers are securely stored and encrypted, just like all other sensitive information.
privacyPolicy.phoneNumbers.item5: You will only receive one SMS per login attempt.
privacyPolicy.rights.title: Your Rights and Choices
privacyPolicy.rights.item1: You may request that we delete your data at any time.
privacyPolicy.rights.item2: You may opt out of SMS by replying STOP to any message. For assistance, reply HELP or contact us at info@thegovlab.org.

landing.greenBanner.title: All children deserve education, regardless of their needs
landing.greenBanner.description: Just like plants, each child learns in their own way. Some need light, some need shade, some bloom quickly, others take time. The AIEP tool helps families care for their child's educational needs.
greenSection.title: AI for IEPs (AIEP) is a free, open-source AI tool built with families to help parents and caregivers understand, translate, and use Individualized Education Programs (IEPs).
greenSection.description1: IEPs are legally binding documents that define the services, supports, and accommodations a student with a disability is entitled to receive. Yet for many families, especially multilingual families, IEPs are difficult to read, navigate, and use as advocacy tools. AIEP exists to change that.
greenSection.description2: AIEP aims to help families move from confusion to clarity, and from passive receipt of information to confident participation in their child's educational journey.
landingContainer.communityCenteredAI.int: AIEP is also a demonstration of community-centered AI in practice.
landingContainer.communityCenteredAI.tex: Most AI systems are built behind closed doors, with rules and assumptions embedded in code or prompts that users never see. In AIEP, many of the system's core instructions are written in plain language and iteratively refined through community feedback, a process the team calls "unboxing the prompt."
This approach allowed families to directly influence how the AI behaves, not just react to its outputs.
landingContainer.communityCenteredAI.sub: Community input shaped decisions such as:
landingContainer.communityCenteredAI.ite: How service minutes are explained in human terms
How strengths are foregrounded before needs
How translations preserve meaning, not just words
How privacy and data protection are handled
landingContainer.communityCenteredAI.con: AIEP shows that AI systems can be transparent, participatory, and accountable, especially in public-interest contexts.
landingContainer.whyAiepExists.title: Why AIEP exists
landingContainer.whyAiepExists.intro: More than 7.5 million students in the United States receive special education services. For each of them, an IEP shapes daily learning experiences and long-term outcomes.
landingContainer.whyAiepExists.subtitle: IEPs are often:
landingContainer.whyAiepExists.item2: Written in technical and legal language
landingContainer.whyAiepExists.item3: Organized in ways that assume professional expertise
landingContainer.whyAiepExists.item4: Inaccessible for families who do not speak English fluently
landingContainer.whyAiepExists.consequen: As a result, families may miss critical details about services, goals, or placements, or struggle to ask informed questions during IEP meetings. These barriers can have real consequences for students.
landingContainer.whyAiepExists.conclusio: AIEP was created in response to what families themselves identified as a systemic problem: the document that governs their child's education is often unreadable to them.
landingContainer.privacyAndTrust.title: Designed for privacy and trust
landingContainer.privacyAndTrust.intro: IEPs contain highly sensitive personal information. From the beginning, families emphasized that privacy was non-negotiable.
landingContainer.privacyAndTrust.subtitl: AIEP is built with privacy-by-design principles, including:
landingContainer.privacyAndTrust.item1: Automated redaction of personally identifiable information
landingContainer.privacyAndTrust.item3: Clear user control over stored information
landingContainer.privacyAndTrust.item4: The ability for families to delete their data at any time
landingContainer.privacyAndTrust.conclus: Trust is earned through design choices that respect users and their data.
landingContainer.privacyAndTrust.diagram: Diagram showing how AIEP protects your privacy: AWS Comprehend detects and removes personal data, then OpenAI creates summaries and translations without storing your information
landingContainer.whatAiepDoes.title: What AIEP does
landingContainer.whatAiepDoes.subtitle: AIEP supports families before, during, and after IEP meetings by helping them:
landingContainer.whatAiepDoes.item1: Translate IEPs into multiple languages while preserving legal and educational meaning
landingContainer.whatAiepDoes.item2: Understand complex terms through plain-language explanations and glossaries
landingContainer.whatAiepDoes.item3: See clear summaries of goals, services, accommodations, and placements
landingContainer.whatAiepDoes.item4: Prepare questions and discussion points for IEP meetings
landingContainer.whatAiepDoes.item5: Navigate IEPs with confidence, not guesswork
landingContainer.whatAiepDoes.conclusion: The tool is designed to surface the specific, legally meaningful details families need to advocate for their child, rather than offering a generic summary.
landingContainer.moreThanATool.title: More than a tool
landingContainer.moreThanATool.intro: While AIEP is a practical resource for families, it is also part of a broader effort to rethink how AI is developed for public systems.
landingContainer.moreThanATool.subtitle: Through AIEP, the team has produced:
landingContainer.moreThanATool.item3: Learning materials for civic AI literacy
landingContainer.moreThanATool.item4: Public writing sharing lessons and failures, not just successes
landingContainer.moreThanATool.conclusio: Together, these resources support families, educators, policymakers, and technologists working to build AI that serves the public good.
landingContainer.builtWithFamilies.title: Built with families, not just for them
landingContainer.builtWithFamilies.intro: AIEP was co-designed with more than 150 parents and caregivers in the San Francisco Bay Area, alongside special education experts and educators.
landingContainer.builtWithFamilies.subti: From the earliest prototypes, families shaped:
landingContainer.builtWithFamilies.item3: What language felt clear, respectful, and empowering
landingContainer.builtWithFamilies.item4: What the tool should not do
landingContainer.builtWithFamilies.codes: Rather than treating families as "end users," AIEP treats them as co-designers and experts in their own lived experience.
landingContainer.builtWithFamilies.concl: This approach reflects a core belief of the project: people most affected by a system should help shape how technology interacts with it.
landingContainer.research.title: Our research questions
landingContainer.research.subtitle: Alongside tool development, we are interested in exploring:
landingContainer.research.item1: How can community members be meaningfully educated about AI so they can participate in its design?
landingContainer.research.item2: What co-design methods are both effective and respectful of families' time and labor?
landingContainer.research.item3: How can community insights be translated into real technical decisions and features?
landingContainer.research.item4: Increase equity in AI design for historically excluded populations?
landingContainer.research.conclusion: Insights from this research inform not only AIEP, but broader conversations about responsible AI in public systems.

landing.howTo.card1.title: Upload an IEP to the tool
landing.howTo.card1.text: After signing up, you will be able to upload your child's IEP document as a document file (doc or docx) or a PDF.
landing.howTo.card2.title: Translate the IEP to your preferred language
landing.howTo.card2.text: Your uploaded IEP will be translated to the language you chose at sign up and will also be available in English.
landing.howTo.card3.title: Get a first glimpse of the entire IEP document
landing.howTo.card3.text: At the top of the screen, you will find a short summary of the information we found on your IEP document.
landing.howTo.card4.title: Understand the main insights from the IEP
landing.howTo.card4.text: In the sections below, you will find the key insights we drew from the document you uploaded. Click on the titles to read the information.
landing.howTo.card5.title: Find the meaning of complex terms
landing.howTo.card5.text: Whenever you see a blue word, you will be able to click on it to show its definition. When you're done, click on the X to return to your summary.
landing.howTo.card6.title: Contrast the content with the original IEP
landing.howTo.card6.text: Below the title of each key insight, you will find the page number where we took the information from. Always double check!
